Composing Kazakh lyrics set to new *dombra* melodies alongside his incisive prose *Book of Words* (*Qara sözder*), Abai urged steppe youths toward science, honest craft and critical self-scrutiny while exposing bribery in colonial township elections—working within volatile nineteenth-century steppe politics long before Soviet and post-independence monuments canonized him as a national icon.
after.zh: 成长于塞米巴拉金斯克近郊成吉思山麓——哈萨克游牧习惯法、沙俄边疆官署与喀山鞑靼经学院交汇之地——阿拜（伊卜拉欣）·库南拜乌勒兼通察合台、波斯、阿拉伯古典诗文，并在塞米巴拉金斯克图书馆结识沙俄流放民粹派学人，译介普希金、莱蒙托夫与克雷洛夫。他既谱写配以冬不拉新调的哈萨克抒情诗，又在散文集《箴言录》（《黑言》）中痛陈殖民乡长选举贿赂与游牧社会积弊，勉励青年治学务实，在十九世纪动荡的草原政局中留下深沉哲思。

items.rationale: Remove "this entry omits inconsistent family claims..." and ground Abai in Semipalatinsk library exiles, dombra songs, and Qara sözder.

before.en:
Queen Soraya Tarzi supported girls’ education and women’s public participation during Amanullah’s reforming reign. Schools, publication and public appearances connected royal action with arguments about family, dress and the possibilities of social change. These initiatives provoked opposition and operated within political relationships that were more complex than a single conflict between progress and tradition.

The collapse of the regime and exile in 1929 interrupted the reform program. Later accounts made Soraya an emblem of women’s advancement, while photographs and institutional records preserve more specific evidence of a public role. This entry focuses on that role rather than choosing among disputed birth-year conventions. Reading it beside Ramabai and later Afghan constitutional history shows that education initiatives could face different constraints and reversals, rather than proceeding along one inevitable path of emancipation.
before.zh:
索拉娅·塔尔齐王后在阿曼努拉改革时期支持女孩教育和女性公共参与。学校、刊物与公开露面，把王室行动同家庭、服饰和社会改变可能性的论辩联系起来。这些举措引起反对，其政治关系也比单一的进步对传统冲突更复杂。

1929年政权崩溃与流亡中断改革计划。后世叙述把她塑为女性进步的象征，照片与机构记录则保存更具体的公共角色证据。本条聚焦这一角色，不在有分歧的出生年份中强作选择。与拉玛拜及后来的阿富汗宪法史并读，可看到教育计划面对不同约束和逆转，而非沿一条必然解放道路前进。

after.en: Born in exile in Damascus into the reformist intellectual household of Mahmud Tarzi and returning to Kabul after 1901, Queen Soraya Tarzi worked beside King Amanullah Khan after Afghanistan won full diplomatic independence in 1919 to build public institutions for women and girls. In 1921 she helped open Masturat—Afghanistan’s first public primary school for girls—co-launched the women’s journal *Ershad-e-Niswan* (*Guidance for Women*) edited by her mother Asma Rasmiya, founded a women’s hospital, and spoke against child marriage and compulsory veiling before conservative rural rebellions and British-frontier intrigues forced the royal couple into European exile in January 1929.
after.zh: 生于大马士革流亡维新思想家马哈茂德·塔尔齐之家、1901年后随父返归喀布尔的索拉娅·塔尔齐王后，在1919年阿富汗赢得外交完全独立后与国王阿曼努拉·汗携手推进现代社会改革。1921年她主持创办阿富汗首所公立女子小学“马斯图拉特”，与母亲阿斯玛合办妇女周刊《妇女指南》（Ershad-e-Niswan），筹建女子医院，并公开倡导废除童婚与强制面纱；1929年1月保守派部族叛乱攻陷喀布尔后，改革骤然中断，王室被迫流亡欧洲。

items.rationale: Cut "This entry focuses on..." and name Damascus/Mahmud Tarzi, 1921 Masturat school, Ershad-e-Niswan, and 1929 exile.

before.en:
Sendler used her work in Warsaw’s welfare system to help Jews under German occupation. Entering the ghetto, finding hiding places and arranging support required cooperation with Jewish activists, other rescuers, institutions and households. Children’s survival depended on a network rather than the actions of one heroic individual alone.

In 1943 she led the children’s section of Żegota, the underground Council for Aid to Jews. Arrest and torture did not end her work after others secured her release. She preserved information about children’s identities and placements, linking rescue with the hope of recovering family ties after the war. Yad Vashem recognized her in 1965. The exact number saved by Sendler and her partners is unknown, so the entry avoids a popular precise total. Her story complements the Holocaust overview by following practical care, danger and cooperation while keeping the persecuted children and their families central.
before.zh:
森德勒利用在华沙福利系统中的工作，帮助德国占领下的犹太人。进入隔都、寻找藏身处和安排援助，需要与犹太活动家、其他救援者、机构及家庭合作。儿童生存依靠一个网络，并非某位英雄个人独自行动的结果。

1943年，她领导地下援犹委员会“热戈塔”的儿童部门。遭逮捕和酷刑后，其他人设法使其获释，她仍继续工作。她保存儿童原有身份与安置地点的信息，把救援与战后恢复家庭联系的希望相连。以色列大屠杀纪念馆于1965年表彰她。森德勒及同伴救出的人数无法精确确定，因此本条不采用流传甚广的精确总数。她的故事通过照护、危险与合作补充大屠杀总览，同时把受迫害儿童及其家庭置于中心。

after.en: Holding a municipal epidemic-control pass from Warsaw’s Social Welfare Department after German occupiers sealed the Warsaw Ghetto in 1940, Polish social worker Irena Sendler (“Jolanta”) coordinated dozens of nurses, tram drivers, Jewish ghetto liaisons, Catholic convents and foster families to smuggle Jewish infants and children past ghetto checkpoints in ambulances, toolboxes and underground courthouse corridors. Appointed head of the children’s section of the underground Council to Aid Jews (*Żegota*) in 1943, she wrote children’s real and assumed names on tissue-thin slips buried in jars beneath an apple tree so surviving relatives might reunite—refusing to betray the network under Gestapo torture at Pawiak Prison before Żegota bribed guards to free her on the day set for her execution.
after.zh: 1940年德军封闭华沙犹太隔都后，波兰市政社会福利局社工伊雷娜·森德勒（地下代号“约兰塔”）凭防疫通行证出入隔都，联合数十名护士、电车司机、隔都犹太联络员、天主教修女院与寄养家庭，借救护车、工具箱及法院地下通道将犹太婴幼儿秘密救出。1943年出任地下援犹委员会“热戈塔”儿童部负责人后，她将受救儿童的真实姓名与寄养住址写在薄纸条上装瓶埋于苹果树下，期盼战后骨肉重逢；被盖世太保捕入帕维亚克监狱施以酷刑折断双足仍严守秘密，终在行刑当日由地下组织重金买通看守虎口脱险（其与同伴救出的确切总人数虽难精准核计，1965年获以色列大屠杀纪念馆授予国际义人称号）。

items.rationale: Turn dry meta-commentary into the gripping Jolanta/Żegota/apple-tree jars/Pawiak Prison rescue story while keeping the headcount qualification intact!

before.en:
Tu Youyou’s research connected pharmaceutical training, historical medical texts and experimental work on malaria. In 1969 she took a leading role in a research group within the wider Project 523 effort. Examining older descriptions of qinghao informed questions about preparation, but the identification of artemisinin also required extraction, testing, chemical work and collaboration across institutions. A traditional reference was a research lead, not by itself proof of a compound’s properties.

The 2015 Nobel Prize recognized her contribution to the discovery. That recognition should be placed beside the collective and institutional history of the research, rather than erasing either individual initiative or the work of colleagues. This entry follows a research career to an award, without treating that award as the end of her life. Her story brings women’s scientific labour and twentieth-century institutions into a history that crossed national boundaries through later recognition and discussion.
before.zh:
屠呦呦的研究把药学训练、历史医籍与疟疾实验联系起来。1969年，她在更广泛的“523”科研工作中担任研究组负责人。对古代青蒿记载的考察，为制备方法提出问题；但青蒿素的发现仍需要提取、实验检验、化学研究和跨机构合作。传统文献提供的是研究线索，并不单独构成对化合物性质的证明。

2015年诺贝尔奖表彰了她对这一发现的贡献。理解这一认可，需要同时保留个人主动性和同事、机构共同工作的历史。本条追踪科研活动至获奖，并不把获奖当作生命终点。她的经历使女性科研劳动与二十世纪的制度进入历史叙述；后续的认可和讨论，又让这一历史跨越国界。

after.en: Trained in pharmacognosy at Beijing Medical College and assigned in January 1969 to head a phytochemical team at the Academy of Traditional Chinese Medicine within China’s nationwide Project 523 antimalarial drive, Tu Youyou screened hundreds of herbal remedies against chloroquine-resistant *Plasmodium* parasites. Noticing a fourth-century instruction in Ge Hong’s *Handbook of Prescriptions for Emergencies* to steep fresh *qinghao* (*Artemisia annua*) in cold water rather than boiling it, Tu switched in 1971 to low-temperature ethyl-ether extraction—isolating crystalline artemisinin with colleagues across cooperating provincial institutes and volunteering among the first human safety subjects before sharing the 2015 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
after.zh: 毕业于北京医学院生药学系、1969年1月受命在中医研究院担任全国抗疟“523任务”中药研究组组长的屠呦呦，率队针对抗氯喹恶性疟原虫筛选数百种方药。受东晋葛洪《肘后备急方》“青蒿一握，以水二升渍，绞取汁”冷浸记载启发，她于1971年改用沸点较低的乙醚冷浸提取工艺，与多省协作科研人员成功分离出青蒿素结晶，并率先以身试药验证临床安全性；这项由个人关键突破与跨机构集体攻关共同造就的成果，使她于2015年获授诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。

items.rationale: Remove "This entry follows a research career..." and highlight Ge Hong’s cold-steeping clue, 1971 ethyl-ether extraction, human trial and Project 523 collaboration.

before.en:
Dolores Huerta’s early organizing connected conditions in agricultural work with the lives of children and families. Born in Dawson, New Mexico, in 1930 and raised mainly in Stockton, California, she trained as a teacher. The hunger and insecurity she encountered among farmworkers’ children helped lead her from the classroom into collective action. In 1955 she became involved in the Community Service Organization, linking local political participation to the needs of working communities.

Huerta co-founded the National Farm Workers Association with César Chávez in 1962. When Filipino workers organized through the Agricultural Workers Organizing Committee began the Delano grape strike in September 1965, the association joined them. The alliance depended on organizing across ethnic and organizational lines; neither a single leader nor a single community explains its achievements. Huerta helped build the boycott beyond the vineyards and negotiated with growers, making consumers and distant supporters part of the struggle.

The 1966 union merger and contracts won in 1970 translated mobilization into more durable institutions. Pay and working conditions were connected to protections, access to care and the practical demands of family life. Huerta also faced gender discrimination while asserting women’s role within the movement. Her work invites attention to the organizing, negotiation and unpaid care behind public demonstrations. This entry follows her formation and the grape-strike years through 1970; that endpoint is a historical focus, not the end of her life or activism.
before.zh:
多洛雷斯·韦尔塔早期的组织工作，把农业劳动条件与儿童、家庭的生活联系起来。她于1930年出生于新墨西哥州道森，主要在加利福尼亚州斯托克顿长大，接受教师训练。农场工人子女的饥饿与生活不稳定，使她从课堂走向集体行动。1955年，她加入社区服务组织的工作，将地方政治参与同劳动社区的需要结合起来。

1962年，她与塞萨尔·查韦斯共同创立全国农场工人协会。1965年9月，农业工人组织委员会中的菲律宾裔工人在德拉诺发起葡萄采收罢工，该协会随后加入。联盟依靠跨族群、跨组织的合作，无法用单一领袖或单一社区解释。韦尔塔推动抵制运动走出葡萄园，并与种植业者谈判，让消费者与远方支持者参与斗争。

1966年的组织合并及1970年赢得的合约，使动员转化为较持久的制度。工资与劳动条件，同保障措施、医疗服务和家庭生活的实际需要相连。韦尔塔还面对性别歧视，同时坚持女性在运动中的地位。她的经历让人看到公共示威背后的组织、谈判与无偿照护劳动。本条关注她的成长及截至1970年的葡萄罢工阶段；结束年份不是她生命或行动的终点。

after.en: Raised in Stockton, California, where watching barefoot farmworkers’ children sit hungry in her elementary classroom convinced her she could do more organizing parents than grading lessons, Dolores Huerta joined Fred Ross’s Community Service Organization in 1955 before co-founding the National Farm Workers Association with César Chávez in 1962. When Filipino table-grape pickers in Larry Itliong’s Agricultural Workers Organizing Committee walked off Delano vineyards in September 1965, Huerta forged the multi-ethnic United Farm Workers alliance, directed the nationwide East Coast consumer grape boycott, and sat across from agribusiness lawyers—negotiating landmark 1970 union contracts covering wages, clean drinking water, rest breaks and pesticide bans while challenging sexism inside and outside the labour movement for decades thereafter.
after.zh: 成长于加利福尼亚州斯托克顿的多洛雷斯·韦尔塔，执教小学时目睹农业季节工子女赤足忍饥上课，毅然走出讲台投身劳工组织：1955年加入社区服务组织，1962年与塞萨尔·查韦斯共创全国农场工人协会。1965年9月拉里·伊特利昂领导的菲律宾裔葡萄采摘工在德拉诺率先罢工后，韦尔塔促成跨族裔联合农场工人公会（UFW），亲赴美东统筹全美消费者抵制葡萄运动，并主笔同大农场主逐条谈判，在1970年签下保障工薪、田间洁净饮水与禁用剧毒农药的历史性工会契约，此后数十年间持续在劳工与妇女平权前线奔走。

items.rationale: Remove "This entry follows her formation..." and add Larry Itliong, East Coast boycott, clean water & pesticide protections.

before.en:
Savitribai Phule’s career joined education to resistance against caste and gender exclusion. Born in 1831 and married as a child, she acquired an education and worked with Jyotirao Phule to develop schooling in Pune. Their work from 1848 made girls’ learning a public challenge to social rules that restricted who could study and teach. It depended on cooperation and local support as well as the persistence of the couple later celebrated as reformers.

Savitribai also wrote. Her 1854 poetry collection, Kavya Phule, belongs beside the classroom in an account of her intellectual life. Education was a means of questioning subordination, not simply of obtaining credentials. The opening of the Phules’ well to people excluded by caste in 1868 brought that principle into the ordinary necessity of obtaining water.

Her activities included relief during famine and care during the Pune plague crisis of 1897, when she died. These episodes connect a life story to the social arrangements that made some people especially vulnerable: limited access to learning, water and care. Later commemorations rightly keep her visible but sometimes disagree on precise dates. This entry uses supported years and avoids treating disputed day-level chronology or broad claims of being India’s first female teacher as settled. Her legacy is better understood through the specific institutions and practices she helped change.
before.zh:
萨维特丽拜·普勒把教育同反对种姓与性别排斥联系起来。她生于1831年，幼年结婚，此后接受教育，并与乔蒂拉奥·普勒在浦那开展办学。自1848年起，他们推动女孩学习，公开挑战限制谁能读书、谁能教学的社会规则。这项工作依靠合作与地方支持，也依靠后来被纪念为改革者的夫妇的坚持。

她同时从事写作。1854年的诗集《卡维亚·普勒》，应与课堂一起纳入其思想生活。教育不仅是取得资格，也是质疑从属地位的工具。1868年，普勒夫妇向因种姓而受排斥的人开放自家水井，把这一原则带入取水这一日常需要。

她的活动还包括饥荒救济，以及1897年浦那鼠疫期间的照护；她也在该年去世。这些经历把个人生平同造成脆弱处境的社会安排连接起来：受教育、用水和获得照护的机会受到限制。后来的纪念文字使她持续受到关注，但部分精确日期相互矛盾。本条采用有支持的年份，不把存在分歧的卒日或“印度第一位女教师”等宽泛说法视为定论。通过她参与改变的具体制度和实践，更能理解其遗产。

after.en: Born into a Mali gardening family in Naigaon in 1831 and taught to read in Pune alongside Fatima Sheikh, Savitribai Phule opened Pune’s Bhide Wada girls’ school with her husband Jyotirao Phule in January 1848—carrying a spare sari in her bag because orthodox passers-by pelted her with mud and cow dung on her walk to class. Publishing anti-caste Marathi verse in *Kavya Phule* (1854), sheltering pregnant Brahmin widows from suicide, and flinging open the Phule household cistern in 1868 to Dalit neighbours barred from public wells, she kept running *Satyashodhak Samaj* schools and famine kitchens after Jyotirao’s death until March 1897, when she contracted bubonic plague after carrying a sick ten-year-old boy on her back to her clinic outside Pune.
after.zh: 1831年生于马哈拉施特拉园艺农家、在浦那与穆斯林同伴法蒂玛·谢赫共修师范的萨维特丽拜·普勒，于1848年1月同丈夫乔蒂拉奥·普勒在浦那创办比德宅院女校——因保守派路人沿街向她投掷泥块牛粪阻挠女学，她每天提着备用纱丽坚持到校授课。她于1854年出版批判种姓压迫的马拉地语诗集《诗花》（Kavya Phule），设立庇护所收留受逼迫寡妇，1868年向被禁触碰公井的“不可接触者”敞开自家水池；1897年浦那鼠疫肆虐时，六十六岁的她亲设疫病诊所，因背负一名染疫男童就医而殉职。

items.rationale: Replace disputed-date meta-boilerplate with Fatima Sheikh, spare sari walk to Bhide Wada, 1868 well opening, and 1897 plague clinic!

before.en:
Nguyễn Thị Bình became internationally visible through the Paris negotiations over the Vietnam War. In 1968 she served as deputy leader of the National Liberation Front’s delegation. She subsequently represented the Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam as foreign minister and delegation leader. Her role illustrates how revolutionary movements sought political recognition through diplomacy as well as through warfare.

She signed the Paris agreement on 27 January 1973. Two pens later donated by her to the Southern Women’s Museum provide a material connection to that act. The objects identify a participant and a moment of negotiation; they do not imply that signing immediately resolved all the conflicts represented at the table. The agreement and Vietnam’s later reunification belong to connected but distinct historical episodes.

Her public career continued after the war. She served as education minister from 1976 to 1987, held senior foreign-affairs responsibilities, and was vice-president from 1992 to 2002. These roles broaden the biography beyond a single widely reproduced photograph of a diplomat signing a document.

Museum displays and official commemorations emphasize courage and national achievement. This entry uses their documented objects and office chronology without treating their praise as an independent evaluation of every policy or negotiation. It follows a bounded public career, not a completed lifespan, and places Paris diplomacy alongside the less visually dramatic work of education and government administration.
before.zh:
阮氏萍通过围绕越南战争的巴黎谈判进入国际公众视野。1968年，她担任民族解放阵线代表团副团长，后来以越南南方共和国临时革命政府外交部长和代表团团长身份参加谈判。她的角色展示革命运动如何既通过战争，也通过外交寻求政治承认。

1973年1月27日，她签署巴黎协定。她后来捐赠给南部妇女博物馆的两支笔，与这一行为建立物质联系。物件能够确认参与者和谈判时刻，却不表示签字立即解决了谈判桌所涉及的全部冲突。协定与越南后来的统一，是相关但不同的历史阶段。

其公共生涯在战后继续。1976至1987年任教育部长，此后担任高级外事职务，1992至2002年任国家副主席。这些工作使传记超越一张被广泛转载的外交官签字照片。

博物馆展览与官方纪念强调勇气及国家成就。本条采用其中有记录的物件与任职年代，不把赞颂视为对每项政策或谈判的独立评价。它聚焦有界限的公共事业，而非完整生卒，并把巴黎外交同视觉上不那么醒目的教育和政府行政工作并置。

after.en: Granddaughter of anticolonial reformer Phan Châu Trinh and schooled in French in Phnom Penh and Saigon before French colonial police jailed her in Chí Hòa Prison from 1951 to 1953, Nguyễn Thị Bình arrived at the Paris Peace Talks in November 1968 as deputy envoy of the National Liberation Front and became foreign minister and chief negotiator of the Provisional Revolutionary Government of South Vietnam in 1969. Across more than four years of gruelling public diplomacy and closed sessions, she became the sole woman among the four plenipotentiaries signing the Paris Peace Accords on 27 January 1973 (later donating her signing pens to Ho Chi Minh City’s Southern Women’s Museum)—though fighting continued until 1975, after which she oversaw postwar school reconstruction as reunited Vietnam’s Minister of Education (1976–1987) and served two terms as Vice President (1992–2002).
after.zh: 作为近代维新先驱潘周桢外孙女、1951—1953年曾因反法活动被囚西贡志和监狱的阮氏萍，于1968年11月赴巴黎出席越战和谈，翌年出任越南南方共和国临时革命政府外交部长兼首席谈判代表。历经四年余折冲樽俎，她于1973年1月27日作为四方全权代表中唯一的女性签署《巴黎和平协定》（所用两支签字笔后捐藏胡志明市南部妇女博物馆）；协定虽未即刻平息延续至1975年的战火，战后她转入国家文教与行政重建，历任统一后越南教育部长（1976—1987）及两届国家副主席（1992—2002）。

items.rationale: Remove "This entry uses their documented objects..." and tell Phan Châu Trinh, Chí Hòa prison, 1973 Paris signing pens, and 1976-2002 career cleanly.

before.en:
Josefa Llanes Escoda’s public life joined teaching, women’s organizations and community service. Teacher training in Manila in 1919 preceded further study in the United States, including Columbia University in 1925. These educational experiences became resources for work at home rather than an isolated personal success story.

She helped develop the Girl Scouts of the Philippines, whose national charter was approved in 1940. The organization gave girls a setting for practical training, cooperation and service. Her involvement in women’s clubs and the campaign for political participation placed this work within a wider movement for women to act in public life. The 1937 suffrage plebiscite belongs to that collective history and cannot be credited to one organizer alone.

During the war and Japanese occupation, Escoda continued support work for fellow Filipinos. She was arrested in August 1944 and imprisoned at Fort Santiago. Accounts record a final sighting in January 1945; the exact circumstances of her killing and burial remain uncertain. A careful biography must preserve that uncertainty rather than turning a last-seen date into a documented execution date.

Later institutional commemorations disagree even on her birth year. This entry therefore follows the better-documented career from training to wartime disappearance. The contrast between school, civic association and prison shows how organized community service could become politically consequential in a colonial society and exceptionally dangerous under military occupation.
before.zh:
何塞法·利亚内斯·埃斯科达的公共生活连接教学、妇女组织与社区服务。1919年在马尼拉接受师资训练后，她又赴美国深造，包括1925年在哥伦比亚大学学习。这些教育经历成为返乡工作的资源，而非孤立的个人成功故事。

她参与发展菲律宾女童军，其全国性组织章程于1940年获批准。组织为女孩提供实用训练、合作与服务的环境。她参与妇女俱乐部及政治参与运动，使这些工作成为女性进入公共生活的更广泛进程的一部分。1937年妇女选举权公投属于集体历史，不能归功于某一位组织者。

战争与日本占领期间，她继续为同胞提供支持。1944年8月被捕，关押于圣地亚哥堡。记述中最后一次见到她是在1945年1月；具体遇害及安葬情况仍不确定。谨慎的传记必须保留这种不确定性，不把最后目击日期改写为已获证实的处决日期。

后来的机构纪念甚至对其出生年也有分歧。因此，本条采用从师资训练至战时失踪的、记录较明确的生涯范围。学校、公民协会与监狱之间的变化，展示有组织的社区服务如何在殖民社会产生政治影响，并在军事占领下变得极其危险。

after.en: Earning her teaching certificate at the Philippine Normal School in Manila in 1919 before completing a master’s degree in social work at Columbia University in 1925, Ilocana civic organizer Josefa Llanes Escoda turned classrooms and women’s clubs into engines of public reform—serving as secretary of the National Federation of Women’s Clubs during the collective campaign that won Filipino women’s suffrage in the 1937 plebiscite, and securing the national charter of the Girl Scouts of the Philippines in May 1940. Under Japanese wartime occupation from 1942, she and her husband Antonio Escoda smuggled medicine, food and messages into Allied POW and civilian internment camps until Kempeitai military police arrested her in August 1944 and locked her in Fort Santiago; fellow prisoners saw her battered but unbroken for the last time in January 1945 during the Battle of Manila, leaving her exact death and unmarked grave unrecorded.
after.zh: 1919年毕业于马尼拉菲律宾师范学校、1925年获美国哥伦比亚大学社会工作硕士的伊洛卡诺女性活动家何塞法·利亚内斯·埃斯科达，归国后任全国妇女俱乐部联合会干事，在汇聚各界力量的1937年菲律宾女性普选权公投运动中奔走呼吁，并于1940年5月推动菲律宾女童军正式获批全国章程。1942年日军占领菲律宾后，她与丈夫安东尼奥秘密向战俘营输送药品、口粮与家书；1944年8月遭日本宪兵队捕入马尼拉圣地亚哥堡，1945年1月马尼拉战役前夕狱友最后一次目睹遍体鳞伤却神色坚毅的她，其遇难确切时日与遗骸安葬处至今成谜。

items.rationale: Remove "A careful biography must preserve..." and "Later institutional commemorations disagree..." while keeping the Jan 1945 last-sighted fact vivid and exact!

before.en:
Alexander grew up in the Macedonian royal household and inherited Philip II’s military resources when he became king in 336 BCE. His expedition into Asia began in 334 BCE and overturned Achaemenid rule. The campaigns linked Macedonia with Egypt, western Asia, Central Asia and the northwestern Indian subcontinent through warfare and new relationships with local rulers. Victory was an exercise in coercion as well as negotiation; the movement of an army should not be read as a peaceful meeting of cultures.

The army’s refusal to continue farther east exposed the limits of royal ambition. Alexander returned west and died in Babylon in 323 BCE. His commanders competed over the inheritance, and successor kingdoms developed rather than one durable, unified state. Later pictures repeatedly retold episodes from his life, including an encounter with the philosopher Diogenes. Such images reveal how later audiences imagined kingship; they are not eyewitness records of the fourth century BCE.
before.zh:
亚历山大在马其顿王室成长，公元前336年即位时继承了腓力二世建立的军事资源。前334年开始的亚洲远征推翻了阿契美尼德王朝的统治。战争和与地方统治者建立的新关系，把马其顿与埃及、西亚、中亚及印度次大陆西北部连接起来。征服既依靠谈判，也依靠强制，不能把军队的推进理解为和平的文化相遇。

军队拒绝继续东进，显露出王权野心的限度。亚历山大返回西方，前323年死于巴比伦。部将争夺遗产，形成多个继业者王国，而非一个稳定统一的国家。后世绘画不断重述他的故事，包括与哲学家第欧根尼的相遇。这些图像说明后人如何想象君王，却不是前四世纪的现场记录。

after.en: Tutored in Macedon’s court circle and succeeding his assassinated father Philip II at twenty in 336 BCE, Alexander III crossed the Hellespont in 334 BCE with veteran phalanxes and Thessalian cavalry to topple Darius III’s Achaemenid Empire across Anatolia, Egypt, Mesopotamia, Iran and Sogdiana—combining calculated marriage diplomacy and Persian court ceremonial with ruthless sieges and mass enslavement at cities such as Thebes and Tyre. Halted at the Hyphasis (Beas) River in 326 BCE when exhausted Macedonians refused to march deeper into India, he retreated through the Gedrosian Desert and died of fever in Babylon in June 323 BCE at thirty-two, leaving generals (the *Diadochi*) to carve rival Hellenistic kingdoms from Egypt to Bactria while centuries of Greek, Persian and European art recast the conqueror into philosophical legend.
after.zh: 少年受教于马其顿王廷、公元前336年父亲腓力二世遇刺后以二十岁即位的亚历山大三世，于前334年率马其顿方阵与色萨利骑兵渡过赫勒斯滂海峡，席卷安纳托利亚、埃及、两河流域、伊朗高原与粟特，推翻大流士三世的阿契美尼德帝国——其间既以政治联姻与波斯宫仪笼络新土贵族，也在底比斯、推罗等抗拒城邦施以屠城与集体贩奴的铁腕。前326年远征军进抵印度河流域比亚斯河畔时因久战疲敝拒绝继续东进，他遂穿越格德罗西亚荒漠西返，于前323年6月在巴比伦热病猝逝（年仅三十二岁）；麾下诸将随即混战瓜分遗业，建立起自托勒密埃及至巴克特里亚的诸多希腊化王国，后世东西方艺文更将其生平演绎为无数王者与哲人传说。

items.rationale: Cut "should not be read as a peaceful meeting..." meta-preaching by showing Thebes/Tyre coercion alongside Persian diplomacy and Hyphasis mutiny directly!

before.en:
Newton entered Trinity College, Cambridge, in 1661. His subsequent investigations of mathematics, motion and light became part of a wider correspondence and institutional world, rather than a single moment of discovery. The Principia, published in 1687 with Edmond Halley’s encouragement, used mathematical reasoning to connect motion and forces. Its preface presents this as a programme of investigation, not a claim that all natural phenomena had already been explained.

Newton’s later working life also belonged to government and learned institutions. He moved to the Royal Mint as warden in 1696, became master in 1699 and president of the Royal Society in 1703. The surviving writings extend well beyond modern physics: the Newton Project includes religious, alchemical and administrative texts alongside mathematical and optical work. These different activities complicate the familiar picture of an isolated genius. His death in 1727 closes this career focus; debates over priority and interpretation continued among later readers.
before.zh:
牛顿于1661年进入剑桥大学三一学院。此后对数学、运动和光的研究，发生在通信交流与学术制度构成的广阔环境中，并非一次孤立的发现。1687年，在爱德蒙·哈雷的鼓励下出版的《自然哲学的数学原理》，用数学推理连接运动与力。其序言把这一方法作为研究纲领，而不是宣称所有自然现象都已得到解释。

牛顿后期的工作也属于政府和学术机构。1696年，他进入皇家铸币局任监督官，1699年成为局长，1703年出任皇家学会会长。传世著述远超现代物理学的范围：牛顿文献计划同时收录宗教、炼金术、行政、数学和光学文本。这些不同活动使“孤独天才”的常见形象变得更加复杂。1727年的死亡结束了本条关注的生涯，优先权和学术解释之争则在后世继续。

after.en: Entering Trinity College, Cambridge, as a subsizar in 1661 and elected Lucasian Professor of Mathematics in 1669, Isaac Newton developed fluxional calculus, decomposed white sunlight with glass prisms, built a reflecting telescope, and—prompted by astronomer Edmond Halley—published *Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica* in 1687, uniting terrestrial falling bodies and planetary orbits under universal gravitation as an open mathematical framework for investigating forces. Moving to London in 1696 as Warden and then Master of the Royal Mint (where he oversaw England’s Great Recoinage and prosecuted counterfeiters) and presiding over the Royal Society from 1703 until his death in 1727, Newton left millions of manuscript words spanning optics, priority disputes with Leibniz and Hooke, chymical furnace notebooks and unorthodox biblical chronology.
after.zh: 1661年以半工读生身份入读剑桥大学三一学院、1669年获聘卢卡斯数学教授的艾萨克·牛顿，创立流数术（微积分）、以三棱镜分解日光、制出反射望远镜，并在天文学家哈雷力促下于1687年出版《自然哲学的数学原理》，用万有引力与运动三定律将地面落体同天体轨道纳入统一的数学推演纲领。1696年他赴伦敦出任皇家铸币局督办及局长（主持英格兰货币重铸并严缉伪币案），1703年起兼任皇家学会会长直至1727年辞世；其传世数百万字手稿除光学与微积分优先权论战外，还密布炼金炉实验记录与圣经年代学考辨，远超后世“纯粹物理学家”的单一画像。

items.rationale: Remove "His death in 1727 closes this career focus" and bring out prisms, reflecting telescope, Mint counterfeiters, Leibniz/Hooke, and chymical manuscripts!

before.en: Li Jing’s career connects the wars that established Tang rule with campaigns beyond its northern and western frontiers. In 621 he helped defeat Xiao Xian’s regime around Jiangling. His forces later struck the Eastern Turkic leadership, contributing to its defeat in 630, and campaigned against Tuyuhun in 635. These were collective military operations involving other commanders, allied forces and defeated communities. Li Jing also held senior posts at court, where military achievement could become political authority. Later generations attached strategic wisdom to his name, but the campaigns can be studied without assuming that every military text attributed to him was actually his work.
before.zh: 李靖的仕途把唐朝建立统治的战争，与其后向北方、西方拓展的战事联系起来。621年，他参与击败以江陵为中心的萧铣政权；630年，其军队打击东突厥统治者，参与东突厥的败亡；635年又出征吐谷浑。这些行动涉及其他将领、协同部队以及战败地区的社会，不能归结为一人的功业。李靖也在朝廷担任要职，军事成就因此转化为政治权威。后世把兵学智慧附着在他的名字上，但研究具体战事，并不需要预先认定所有托名兵书都出自其手。

after.en: Initially an official under the Sui who nearly lost his head before Li Shimin intervened, strategist Li Jing (571–649) became early Tang China’s pre-eminent field commander across both riverine and steppe theatres: floating fleets down the Yangtze Gorge during autumn floods in 621 to capture Xiao Xian’s southern capital at Jiangling, leading a fast winter cavalry strike across snowbound Yinshan in 630 that shattered Illig Qaghan’s Eastern Turkic camp in concert with Li Shiji’s columns, and marching past Qinghai Lake at age sixty-four in 635 to defeat Tuyuhun forces. Serving afterward as chancellor at Chang’an while guarding against court suspicion, his campaigns inspired later Tang and Song military dialogues such as *Duke Li of Wei’s Questions and Replies*—works compiled centuries after his lifetime rather than written by his own brush.
after.zh: 初仕隋室、险遭处斩而获李世民保下的名将李靖（571—649），在唐初南北迥异的战场上屡建奇功：621年乘秋汛率水陆大军出三峡直捣江陵，平定萧铣割据政权；630年正月冒严寒率精骑奇袭阴山定襄、白道，与李勣诸路并进击溃东突厥颉利可汗牙帐；635年又以六十四岁高龄统军越青海湖远征吐谷浑。凯旋入朝任尚书右仆射等宰辅重职后，他深居简出化解猜忌；后世流传的《唐太宗李卫公问对》等兵书则系唐宋兵家借其战绩纂辑而成，并非李靖亲笔遗著。
